title: Sector Lead (Telecommunications Media Technology) Directed Content
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>About AlphaSense: </strong></h2> <p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit <span><a href="http://www.alpha-sense.com" target="_blank">www.alpha-sense.com</a></span>. Come join us.</span></p></div><p><strong>About Expert Insights:</strong><br>Expert Insights, which spans AlphaSense’s Expert Transcript Library and 1x1 Call Services offerings,<span class="Apple-converted-space">  </span>delivers a new and transformative form of market intelligence content. Through transcripts covering thousands of companies, it captures the unfiltered views and insights of business operators in the trenches, interviewed by professional investors who drill into key questions on what’s truly important about a company at each moment in time. AlphaSense’s library of over 220,000 transcripts is the market’s largest, covering all sectors of the economy, with thousands more published each month. Expert Insights is quickly becoming a table-stakes solution for institutional investors to choose the right companies to invest in while gaining rapid adoption among all other consumers of market intelligence from sell-side research and banking, consultancies, and large corporations.</p> <p><strong>About the Team:</strong></p> <p>The Directed Content Team is an integral part of the Expert Insights group, generating thousands of calls each quarter on high-value and strategic content targets - ensuring that the AlphaSense Expert Transcript Library (ETL) delivers comprehensive coverage to our users. The Directed Content team is responsible for identifying, recruiting, and onboarding the best possible experts from around the world based on the targets and topics we are looking to generate content against - ensuring that the interviews with those experts are of the highest-possible quality and relevance.</p> <p><strong>About the Role:<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></strong></p> <p>As a Sector Lead on our TMT (Technology, Media and Telecoms) Directed Content team, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring AlphaSense delivers the highest-quality proprietary research content within your assigned sector. Reporting to the Director of Research (TMT) you will oversee the day-to-day execution of Directed Content projects, ensuring all work meets the firm’s standards for quality, relevance, and, end-user value delivery. As Sector Lead, you will manage coverage of EMEA and APAC companies.</p> <p>You will combine operational rigor with sector expertise to oversee a team of Project Managers responsible for generating expert call transcripts across a diverse range of topics within your coverage universe. Your responsibilities will span project setup, expert sourcing guidance, transcript quality assurance, budget oversight, and performance management. Acting as the connective layer between the Director of Research’s strategic vision and day-to-day execution, you will ensure flawless delivery of sector coverage plans while maintaining a pulse on emerging market themes and client information needs.</p> <p>You will also serve as a key stakeholder in developing and optimizing project workflows, implementing structured QA and feedback loops, and partnering with Product and Operations teams to pilot new AI-enabled tools that elevate both efficiency and insight quality.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do:</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p> <ul> <li>Partner with<span class="Apple-converted-space">  </span>the Director of Research to develop and maintain a strategic sector roadmap, which you will then translate into a structured execution plan, ensuring coverage aligns with key market and client priorities.</li> <li>Manage and mentor a team of Project Managers that oversee the execution of Directed Content projects, setting clear goals, tracking KPIs, and ensuring accountability across all deliverables.</li> <li>Collaborate with Operations Managers who oversee Analyst execution of expert recruiting, onboarding, and interaction facilitation to align operational KPIs to coverage strategy and optimize execution</li> <li>Own expert budget management for your sector, allocating resources effectively to maximize content ROI while maintaining high quality and throughput.</li> <li>Oversee a structured QA process for ensuring transcripts within your sector of coverage meet the highest standards for data accuracy, relevance, structure, and analytical depth.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with the Director of Research and our Content Strategy Analyst to monitor engagement data, identify coverage gaps, and recalibrate project pipelines accordingly.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with the Director of Research to identify and shape content to support revenue-generating efforts such as white papers, webinars, internal and external presentations.</li> <li>Establish and maintain feedback loops with call takers and project teams to enhance the quality and insight of future content.</li> <li>Collaborate with North America directed content teams to ensure high quality output and consistency.</li> <li>Partner with Operations and Product teams to pilot and optimize AI-enabled tools that improve project throughput, QA precision, and overall efficiency.</li> <li>Maintain deep familiarity with ongoing developments within the Healthcare, TMT or Energy & Industrial sectors, proactively surfacing new themes and companies to guide future research focus.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who You Are:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have 5–7 years of experience in equity research, market intelligence, consulting, or a related analytical role within TMT</li> <li>You bring deep domain expertise in Technology, Media & Telecoms with a strong grasp of the key players, business models, and industry trends shaping your space.</li> <li>You have a strong understanding of European and Asian equity markets.</li> <li>You have proven people management experience, successfully leading, mentoring, and developing teams of project managers or analysts.</li> <li>You are skilled at translating strategic objectives into actionable research projects that yield high-impact insights.</li> <li>You possess exceptional organizational, analytical, and critical-thinking skills, able to balance multiple priorities with agility while maintaining high quality standards.</li> <li>You have a strong command of project economics, capable of managing budgets, optimizing expert costs, and tracking ROI to ensure resource efficiency.</li> <li>You are adept at working cross-functionally with Directors of Research, Go-to-Market, Product, and Compliance to ensure alignment and continuous improvement.</li> <li>You are intellectually curious, client-oriented, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.</li> <li>You maintain a strong understanding of compliance, MNPI, and confidentiality standards across all project types.</li> </ul> This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Recruiting Scams and Fraud</span></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. description: <p><strong>Corporate & Growth Strategy</strong><br><strong>Grade: Engagement Lead & Engagement Director</strong><br><strong>Location: London (UK) </strong></p> <p><strong>About Alpha FMC</strong><br>Alpha FMC is a leading global consulting firm focused exclusively on serving clients in the Financial Services sector. Our 1,500+ consultants work across 19 offices globally, combining deep FS sector expertise with high-quality consulting to support more than 970 clients across asset management, wealth management, insurance and broader financial services.<br>Our Strategy & Deals division advises the leadership teams of leading financial institutions and high-growth businesses on their most important strategic decisions.<br>We are continuing to grow our Corporate Strategy practice and are recruiting experienced strategy consultants at Engagement Lead and Engagement Director level.</p> <p><strong>The opportunity</strong><br>This is a senior corporate strategy role, combining complex problem-solving, engagement leadership, and practice-building.<br>Our work spans corporate and business-unit strategy, growth strategy and market entry, value creation, and strategic operating model and cost questions for both corporate and sponsor-backed clients. Engagements require teams to structure complex problems into clear hypotheses and develop the market, customer, competitor, financial and operational evidence to validate them.<br>Alpha is a specialist consulting firm and Corporate Strategy is a priority growth area within our Strategy & Deals division. You will have scope to help build the practice by developing client relationships, establishing areas of market focus, shaping propositions, and building the team, with increasing responsibility at the Engagement Director level.<br>You will also work closely with colleagues across Alpha's wider consulting business, combining strategy consulting capability with deep sector and functional expertise to bring clients integrated teams and distinctive advice.</p> <p><strong>Our work</strong><br>We help leading financial institutions and sponsor-backed businesses make their most important strategic decisions. Our work spans financial services, with a primary focus on asset management, wealth management, insurance and fintech.<br>Engagements we typically lead include:<br>•    Developing corporate, business-unit and growth strategies for established financial institutions and scaling businesses<br>•    Assessing new markets, customer segments, products and distribution opportunities, and shaping market entry and expansion plans<br>•    Reviewing propositions, commercial models and competitive positioning<br>•    Evaluating inorganic and partnership routes to growth, including where they are a better answer than building organically<br>•    Addressing strategic operating model and organisational questions<br>•    Supporting sponsor-backed businesses with value creation strategy, including growth, pricing, commercial effectiveness, cost reduction, operating model and other post-close strategic priorities<br>•    Translating strategy into clear priorities, investment cases and plans that management teams can act on</p> <p><strong>Key responsibilities</strong><br>Both Engagement Leads and Engagement Directors are expected to lead complex strategy engagements independently. description: About OLIX AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The Role As a Staff Embedded Software Engineer, you will be the design authority for a major area of the DX-1 platform firmware, within the overall platform architecture. This is the software that makes a rack of custom silicon bootable, manageable and observable, from pre-silicon simulation and FPGA prototypes through first silicon into production. The kind of work you would own: bare-metal and real-time firmware on resource-constrained cores, embedded Linux on the platform processors, the BMC and management plane, and register-level control of the ASIC over its management link. You will report to the Platform Architect who leads the Embedded team and work closely with the FPGA, ASIC and Systems Software teams. You bring exceptional depth on both sides of the hardware-software boundary, the judgment to identify what matters most and why, and the ability to influence and align engineering teams without relying on formal authority. We will judge it by what others can build on: specs other teams work to, firmware that is ready when the hardware is, and designs that still hold up a year on. Responsibilities Lead a major area of the platform firmware. Boot and update, platform management or register-level control of the ASIC, agreed with you based on your strengths. Own its design, interfaces and roadmap within the platform architecture, and be accountable for it reaching production. Make the interfaces explicit. Write down the contracts your area depends on and exposes, from register maps to update and telemetry flows, so the teams on either side can build against them. Support bring-up and validation. When a bring-up or test problem turns out to be in boot, drivers or the management plane, you are the person who gets called. Help the teams running it get to the cause, and write up what you find so nobody has to rediscover it. Define failure and update behaviour. How a fault in a node, rail or link is contained so it does not take out the rack, what gets logged so we can find the cause, and what happens if a firmware update is interrupted halfway. Build things the team keeps using. Reference implementations, firmware tests on the infrastructure the validation teams already run, and contributions to the device models. Pick the problems that matter. Identify the highest-impact technical risks in the platform firmware and at its interfaces to the FPGA and silicon teams, and make sure they get solved. Develop the senior engineers around you. Review their designs as well as their code, set them up to lead areas of their own, and take an active part in hiring. Skills & Experience Depth on both sides of the hardware-software boundary. Bare-metal or RTOS firmware on resource-constrained cores, and embedded Linux BSP work (Yocto/OpenEmbedded, U-Boot or UEFI, drivers, device tree). Systems fundamentals. Memory ordering and barriers, coherent and non-coherent shared memory, synchronisation with and without atomics, interrupt latency, and timing and memory-bandwidth budgets. Taken firmware through a silicon or board bring-up, from pre-silicon simulation or emulation and FPGA prototypes to first power-on, and able to walk us through what went wrong and how it was found. More than one generation, or firmware for an ASIC whose tape-out you worked towards, is a significant advantage. Platform management in a rack-scale context. OpenBMC or equivalent, Redfish, PLDM over MCTP, and the buses underneath (I2C/SMBus/PMBus, SPI, UART), including power sequencing and fault isolation. Register-level control of an ASIC or large FPGA over a management link, including against a simulation model before silicon exists. Precision timing (IEEE 1588 PTP, White Rabbit, SyncE), SerDes or optical link bring-up, or secure boot would all be an advantage. Technical leadership without formal authority. A specification, methodology, or tool you authored that teams outside your own adopted and still use, and the design document behind it. Outstanding technical communicator. You can articulate architectural decisions and their consequences clearly to engineers, managers and senior leadership alike, and write design documents that other teams build to. They don't stop at recommendations: they make the changes too, at the level of control each brand chooses. It works inside Slack, plugs into 100+ tools from Shopify and NetSuite to Meta, Google and Amazon, and is running 23 brands today across paid media, retention, inventory and wholesale, stores, marketplaces, catalog and partnerships. Every function has a tool. Nothing runs the whole. We built SuperchargeMe to run the whole. The product is live and brands are paying for it. Getting it in front of the right brands is the next step. That's you. The role in a sentence Be our first marketer and own the go-to-market: fill the sales calendar with CEOs, CFOs, COOs, CMOs and VPs of E-Commerce at mid-market omnichannel brands, and grow the brands that sign up on their own. Where we are SuperchargeMe is already revenue-generating, with brands paying for it every month. What it doesn't have yet is a way for the next hundred brands to find it. Who we sell to: mid-market omnichannel brands in the US, UK and EU, selling across their own store, marketplaces, wholesale and retail. Two ways in: brands starting with a single product sign up and get going on their own. Brands that want several platforms working together, with onboarding, book a demo. There's no marketing team, agency or playbook yet. You start with a live website, a sales deck, a product you can demo, and case studies from our first clients that are being written now. A founding Account Executive starts alongside you, so every demo you book has a closer waiting, while sign-ups go straight into the product. The story is ready to tell. Brands run ten to twenty tools, each now with its own AI, and none of them agree. We call it the Silo Tax. Naming it, and making brand leaders feel it, is the heart of this job. The work Set the go-to-market plan: which buyers and markets we go after first, and through which channels. Run paid media yourself across Meta, Google, LinkedIn and anything else that works, alongside email, retargeting, campaigns aimed at named brands, events, and joint marketing with agencies, Shopify partners and systems integrators. Work out which of our ten products to lead with for each type of buyer, and write the messaging for each. Build and look after the route to a demo: landing pages, the booking flow, qualifying questions, quick follow-up and a clean handover to sales. Grow self-serve sign-ups, from the first visit to an account that's actually using the product, including our Shopify App Store listing. Turn our case studies and the founders' experience into posts, pages and short videos. Use our own agents on your campaigns, starting with Ads-IQ on Google and Meta. Report every week on demos, sign-ups, activation, pipeline and what each one cost. What good looks like We'll measure you on qualified demos and sign-ups, and the revenue they lead to. Clicks, impressions and ROAS only matter as far as they get us there. After your first month, tracking is set up properly, you've agreed the list of target brands with sales, and your first campaign is running. After your first quarter, demos and sign-ups come in every week from channels you set up, and you know what each one costs by channel. Sales starts asking for more of one kind of lead, because those are the deals that close. The case studies already being written with our first clients are published, and sales uses them in every deal. What you bring At least four years in B2B demand generation or growth, ideally at a software company selling to e-commerce or retail brands. You've run Meta, Google and LinkedIn campaigns yourself, including campaigns aimed at a list of named companies, without an agency doing it for you. You can show the pipeline or sign-ups you've been responsible for, and what they cost. You write well enough that a CMO reads to the end. You build your own reporting in the CRM and analytics tools. You already use AI tools and agents in your day-to-day work and can show us how. We sell AI agents, so we'd expect that. You're comfortable being the first and only marketer for a while. Bonus points You've run a DTC or e-commerce brand. You've built demand from zero at an early-stage B2B company. You've run events or executive dinners in commerce or retail. Skip this one if Your best campaigns needed an agency to run them. You report clicks and impressions and call it pipeline. You'd rather write the plan than ship the campaign. You want a remote or mostly remote role. We're together in North London Monday to Thursday. Why join You'll set up marketing from scratch, and you'll have a say in who joins the team after you. Most brand leaders haven't yet seen AI that takes actions on their business. You'll shape how they first hear about it. You'll work alongside both founders, who ran commerce brands before building software. Decisions are quick, and what you hear from the market gets into the product fast. You can use our agents on your own work from your first day. How we hire A 30-minute intro call with the co-founders. A short exercise: a one-page plan for getting qualified demos from mid-market omnichannel brands and growing sign-ups. A working session with the founders on your plan. References. What you get £60,000–£75,000 salary plus bonus Share options so you own a real piece of what you build. Plus a company car and a strong benefits package. In person in North London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays flexible Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Founder's Associate Intern
description: We're hiring a Founder's Associate intern at Listo. 🚀 Listo is an AI workforce for hospitality. We make hotels discoverable and bookable inside AI, then put agents to work across the hotel on the workflows that move the P&L: revenue, guest communication and operations. We're a small team in London, already working with hotel groups. Now we need someone to help us grow. What you'll work on Growth and business development: events, conferences and partners. Finding the rooms we should be in, and getting us into them. Marketing and content: pushing our story out and turning what we build into content people actually read. Everything in between. It's a generalist role, and no two weeks will look the same. Who we're looking for Early in your career. Some experience in a startup, consulting, VC or marketing is a plus. A self-starter. What you get You work directly with the founders, on everything. Real responsibility from week one. The goal is for this to become a full-time role within 3 to 6 months. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Telnyx</strong></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a </span></em><a href="https://telnyx.com/our-network"><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">private, global, multi-cloud IP network</span></em></a><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">, to bringing </span></em><a href="https://telnyx.com/resources/about-edge-connectivity"><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">hyperlocal edge</span></em></a><em><span style="font-weight: 400;"> technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications.</span></em></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.</span></em></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.</span></em></p></div><p> </p> <h2><strong>The opportunity</strong></h2> <p>We're looking for a Director or VP of Product Marketing to lead that effort globally. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect deep technical understanding with positioning, distribution and commercial results. The title will reflect the experience and scope of the person we hire.</p> <p>A good product story matters, but a story alone isn't enough. The person in this role needs to turn our infrastructure into clear customer problems we solve, compelling reasons to choose Telnyx and practical ways to try it. A great sample application, integration or reference architecture can do more than another 30-slide deck. So can a precise message that reaches a developer at the moment they are deciding how to build.</p> <p>You'll work across Product, Engineering, Developer Relations, Sales and Marketing to bring those pieces together. You'll help shape what we launch, how we explain it, how buyers discover it and how our field teams take it to market.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll build</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A coherent product story. Own positioning, segmentation and competitive differentiation across AI inference, Voice AI, agent and edge infrastructure, communications, networking and wireless. Make the full platform understandable without flattening the technical details that make it valuable.</li> <li>Solutions people can actually use. Drive the packaging of sample apps, reference architectures, integrations, templates and working demos that prove what the infrastructure makes possible. Build repeatable plays for use cases such as contact centers, agent assist and industry-specific workflows. These should accelerate adoption and enterprise sales, not become disconnected software products.</li> <li>Distribution that reaches technical buyers. Shape how we win discovery through product pages, developer content, SEO, answer engine optimization (AEO), technical communities and paid acquisition. You won't necessarily operate every campaign, but you must understand the mechanics deeply enough to direct them: search and answer-engine visibility, technical site structure, intent, targeting, conversion paths, attribution and economics.</li> <li>A field-ready commercial engine. Give enterprise sellers, FDEs and solutions teams the pitches, discovery frameworks, architecture diagrams, competitive proof, demos and ROI narratives they need to generate and advance opportunities. Translate platform capabilities into buying reasons for developers, technical executives and enterprise decision-makers.</li> <li>Launches that translate into adoption. Work with Product and Engineering early, not after something ships. Choose the audience, packaging and launch strategy, then measure activation, qualified demand, field utilization and downstream pipeline. Build an operating cadence that keeps pace with a rapidly changing roadmap.</li> <li>An AI-native PMM team. Use AI research tools, coding assistants, agents and automation as part of everyday work to accelerate market research, competitive analysis, messaging tests, content production, demo development and go-to-market execution. Know when to trust those tools, how to evaluate outputs and where human technical judgment still matters. Lead the team to operate the same way.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>How we'll measure success</strong></h2> <p>The ultimate measure is pipeline. Not the number of launches, assets, impressions or campaigns. We expect this leader to partner closely with Demand Generation and Sales to create measurable, qualified pipeline, improve conversion and accelerate opportunities. Product marketing should be able to show how specific product narratives, solutions, integrations and programs contribute to commercial results.</p> <p>Early wins will look like a dramatically clearer platform story; a small number of flagship use cases with runnable demos and integrations; sellers using consistent, technically credible plays; stronger discovery and conversion from search, AEO and paid channels; and a repeatable link from product launches to adoption and pipeline. We care about what works and scales, not activity for its own sake.</p> <h2><strong>What we're looking for</strong></h2> <ul> <li>You've led product marketing for a complex B2B technical platform, ideally in AI infrastructure, developer tools, APIs, cloud, networking or communications. You can be strategic without becoming removed from the work.</li> <li>You are technically fluent. You can understand architecture, work with APIs or SDKs, interrogate a latency or cost claim and talk comfortably with engineers. You don't have to be a production engineer, but you need to know when a demo is real and when it's just a pitch.</li> <li>You understand modern technical acquisition. You're credible directing AEO, SEO, paid programs and developer-focused content, and can connect channel-level metrics to funnel economics and qualified pipeline.</li> <li>You're already effective with AI tools and agents in your own work. You experiment, build workflows and use the technology to move faster. Familiarity with the limitations and evaluation of AI-generated outputs is as important as enthusiasm for the tools.</li> <li>You write exceptionally well, have strong instincts for enterprise sales, and know how to turn a complex product advantage into a clear reason to buy.</li> <li>You've built or led strong teams, can prioritize across competing launches and products, and enjoy working directly with product leaders and technical builders.</li> </ul> <p>Telecom experience is not required. Technical curiosity, taste, speed and a track record of generating commercial impact matter more.</p> <h2><strong>Why Telnyx</strong></h2> <p>This is a chance to shape the market narrative for a company that owns the underlying network, communications and compute infrastructure it sells. The platform is real, customers are deploying it in production, and the commercial opportunity is substantial. You'll have direct access to senior leadership and the ability to build a PMM function measured by its contribution to growth.</p> <h4><strong>Equal opportunity</strong></h4> <p>Telnyx is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from different backgrounds and evaluate candidates based on the skills and experience relevant to the role.</p> <h3><span style="font-weight: 400; font-size: 14px;">#LI-RH1</span></h3><div class="content-conclusion"><p> </p> <p> </p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. What the job actually feels like This is a build job. When you join, BLP has no UK pipeline, no UK case studies, and no local playbook. It’s not the well-oiled machine with sophisticated processes for everything. What you get instead: an experienced Account Executive sitting next to you, a reporting line to the VP of Business Development and a strong DACH SDR team behind you. You get a winning product and a market nobody here has sold into yet. All of that comes with strong support from the Switzerland HQ. Your first job is to work out who buys, why, and what makes them pick up the phone. You will hear no far more often than yes. The yes is a 30-minute discovery call with a CFO, COO, or Head of Finance at a large UK manufacturer or industrial business, where you run the meeting, present the value, and map the stakeholders live. If you want a finished machine to plug into, this is the wrong role. If you want to help build the machine, read on. About the role As our Founding SDR in London, you own outbound into UK enterprise accounts. You will prospect and open relationships with Finance and Procurement leaders (CFO, COO, Head of Shared Services, Process Excellence, AP) and generate qualified opportunities for our agentic AI platform automating Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash. Don’t expect inbounds to carry you from day one. You are one of the first commercial hires on the ground in a new market. You prospect, you run the connect calls, and you help write the playbook the next UK hires will use. You report directly to the VP of Business Development for now, work day to day with the UK Account Executive as a tag-team, and lean on the DACH SDR team for what already works. You will monitor the UK market with regards to procurement and finance processes, ERP transformation announcements and buying triggers, and turn what you learn into better targeting. We need you to flag what is not working early and bring it to the team, so we fix the approach fast instead of grinding on a broken one. Once the UK team reaches critical mass and shows initial success, we hire a local team lead (internally or externally). You’ll create impact for our future by taking ownership, contributing to shared goals and helping shape what comes next, all as part of our enhanced international community of talented, collaborative and passionate teams. The difference you’ll make You’ll sit in the Commercial Finance team, reporting to the Head of Finance Business Partnering. You’ll work closely with senior operational and commercial leaders across the organisation as a dedicated financial co-pilot to evaluate growth opportunities, manage capital deployment, and guide strategic decision-making. Together, the team will design financial frameworks, process analytics, and robust commercial models that directly drive our competitive advantage and long-term performance. Through clear frameworks, trusted partnerships and practical guidance, we support better decisions, manage risk and create strong foundations for sustainable growth. Your day-to-day: Act as a trusted financial co-pilot to leadership teams, providing insightful analysis, commercial evaluation, and constructive challenge to drive optimal business outcomes. Understand and translate performance drivers, connecting operational metrics with trading performance to deliver actionable insights and commercial recommendations. Build influential relationships across business functions, embedding yourself to become the go-to expert for financial matters, deal structuring, and strategic negotiations. Develop and own robust financial frameworks for major investment initiatives, managing the process from initial financial due diligence and business case preparation through to post-investment review. Evaluate risk and build business cases, collaborating with cross-functional teams to structure commercial arrangements and present recommendations to executive leadership. Establish tracking and performance reporting to monitor capital deployment against budget, evaluate deal performance, and measure overall strategy effectiveness. Demonstrable success in a commercial finance business partnering or FP&A role, ideally within a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Experience working with high volumes of complex data with the aptitude to distil granular detail and convey simple, clear insights to stakeholders. Comfortable with ambiguity and thrives on the challenge of building out new processes and capabilities in a 'greenfield' setting. Clear understanding of key profitability levers, commercial deal structures, and financial governance. Exceptional communication skills with a proven ability to influence, support, and constructively challenge senior non-finance leaders. As we continue to grow and evolve, we want everyone to feel supported and able to do their best work. We’re also committed to making our hiring process accessible, so please let our Talent Acquisition team know if you need any adjustments at any stage. Your manager will meet with you regularly to agree goals, offer feedback and discuss your development, including time for learning.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">We welcome different perspectives and make space for everyone to contribute. As you take on more responsibility, your colleagues will help you work through challenges, and your ideas will be listened to and discussed respectfully.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <h3>How you’ll learn and grow</h3> <p>Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build performance engineering skills through hands-on work on compute kernels, benchmarks and tests.<span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Profiling and experiments will help you understand where time is spent and how changes to code and data layout affect performance. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned.</p> <p>Coursework or experience with machine learning frameworks, parallel programming, code optimisation, maths libraries or performance analysis would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements.</p> <h3>Benefits</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Flexible working:</strong> Find a balance between your internship and life outside work</li> <li><strong>5 days of annual leave:</strong> Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship</li> <li><strong>Life in the office:</strong> Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista</li> <li><strong>Learning and development:</strong> Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform</li> </ul> <p>We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.</p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.</p> <h3>Introduction to Graphcore</h3> <p>At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.<br>Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.</p> <h3>How to apply and what to expect </h3> <p>To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.</p> <p>Curious about where your skills could take you? <strong>Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.</strong></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Product Specialist Partner Solutions Architect
description: <p>A newly created role to help Databricks create new product categories. As Databricks accelerates its most strategic products, we are investing ahead of the curve in the partner ecosystem that helps our customers adopt them, and we are building a new specialisation function to lead that effort. You will pioneer it across EMEA.</p> <p>Reporting to: Director, Partner Field Engineering (EMEA).</p> <p>As the Senior Product Specialist Partner Solutions Architect, you own how our leading System Integrator partners develop deep, market-leading expertise in Databricks' priority products:</p> <ul> <li><strong>OLTP/Postgres (Lakebase):</strong> Databricks' fully managed, Postgres-compatible operational (OLTP) database for intelligent applications</li> <li><strong>Product AI (Genie):</strong> Databricks' natural-language analytics experience, letting anyone ask questions of governed data conversationally</li> <li><strong>AI Router & Governance (Unity Gateway):</strong> Databricks' governed gateway for securely managing, monitoring and routing access to AI and large language model endpoints</li> <li><strong>Migrations & Modernisation:</strong> moving legacy data warehouses and platforms onto the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform</li> <li><strong>Turn-key Solutions:</strong> Cybersecurity (Lakewatch) and CDP (CustomerLake) with more to come</li> </ul> <p>Your mandate is to take our leading partners to the highest tier of Centre-of-Excellence product specialisation on these products, and to turn them into independent, market-leading extensions of the Databricks field. Working hand in hand with our EMEA Product Specialist team, you will carry both the deep technical narrative and the business-value and go-to-market narrative that get these products positioned, adopted and scaled through the partner channel. This is a builder's role: you will design the blueprint for a partner product-specialist function that Databricks scales globally, starting in EMEA.</p> <h2><strong>What we are trying to achieve</strong></h2> <p>Databricks' priority products are seeing strong momentum across EMEA. Lakebase is one of the fastest-growing additions to our platform, Unity Gateway is newly generally available, and AI/BI + Genie are changing how customers work with their data. As adoption accelerates, our partners are central to helping customers realise value quickly and at scale. Deepening partner expertise in these products is one of the most powerful levers we have to accelerate customer time-to-value, and this role exists to build that capability deliberately and ahead of demand, so our partners lead the market.</p> <h2><strong>What the role owns</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Building the partner specialist community (the day-to-day).</strong> Select, enable and certify leading EMEA partners to the highest tier of product specialisation, running the enablement engine end to end: partner selection, technical upskilling to expert depth, certification and first joint customer wins.</li> <li><strong>Partnering with our Product Specialist team.</strong> Act as the partner-side counterpart to Databricks' EMEA Product Specialists, bringing the latest product expertise to partners, connecting partner enablement to live customer opportunities, and channelling partner and customer adoption insight back to our product organisation.</li> <li><strong>Scaling specialist capacity through partners.</strong> Grow models where specialised partners bring product-specialist capacity to joint customers, so expertise scales across the ecosystem.</li> <li><strong>Launch-partner motions.</strong> Position specialised partners as launch partners for major product releases, signalling ecosystem trust and accelerating go-to-market at each milestone.</li> <li><strong>Thought leadership and the business-value narrative.</strong> Author the "better-together" technical and commercial story for these products in the partner channel: reference architectures, positioning, partner offers and value framing that let partners sell and deliver independently. Be a visible voice for partner product specialisation, internally and externally.</li> <li><strong>Building the function.</strong> Define the operating model, the specialisation and certification criteria, the partner selection bar and the cadence, and create the template Databricks adopts to scale this function worldwide.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>The impact you will have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Accelerate customer adoption and time-to-value on Databricks' priority products by putting genuine product depth into the partner channel.</li> <li>Grow partner-led momentum behind our fastest-growing products, building partner capability ahead of the demand curve.</li> <li>Elevate leading EMEA System Integrators to full independence on the priority products, so they operate as market leaders and true extensions of the Databricks field.</li> <li>Establish a repeatable, globally scalable partner product-specialist function, proven in EMEA and exported across Databricks.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What we look for</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Extensive hands-on experience with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, with genuine depth in at least two of the priority products above and the ability to get to depth quickly on the rest. This is a senior role for an established Databricks expert.</li> <li>Proven ability to build partner or field capability at scale: enablement, certification and community-building that turns others into independent experts.</li> <li>Strong business-value and go-to-market instinct: able to translate technical depth into commercial positioning and partner-led market impact, and to engage partner and customer organisations at senior-executive level.</li> <li>Demonstrated thought leadership: authoring technical and business content (reference architectures, solution guides, positioning, playbooks) and presenting complex products credibly to technical and executive audiences.</li> <li>At least 5 years of technical pre-sales or sales-methodology experience in a consumption business model, and experience designing and delivering end-to-end data, warehousing and AI architectures.</li> <li>Coding experience in a core language (Python, SQL, Java or Scala) and hands-on experience building data applications or AI agents.</li> <li>The maturity to build a new function from the ground up: defining the operating model, standards and cadence, and managing multiple changing priorities across a partner ecosystem and internal teams.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have:</strong> System Integrator or consulting background; experience with transactional databases (e.g. PostgreSQL) and application development; experience with LLM gateways, AI governance or AI security; experience running partner specialisation, certification or champion programmes; additional European languages.</p> <p>The role requires up to 40% travel across EMEA, to partner sites, Databricks offices and key industry events.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>About Databricks</strong></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, sans-serif;">Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/databricks">LinkedIn</a>, <a href="https://x.com/databricks">X</a>, <a href="https://www.youtube.com/@Databricks">YouTube</a>, and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/databricksinc/?hl=en">Instagram</a>.<br><br><strong>Benefits<br><br></strong></span>At Databricks, we strive to provide comprehensive benefits and perks that meet the needs of all of our employees. For specific details on the benefits offered in your region click <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/154un3e8Xav4BceOSlcYFZRGEuQI54xMxVydRwQn54eQ/edit?usp=sharing">here</a>.<br><br></p> <p><strong>Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion</strong></p> <p>At Databricks, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can excel. We take great care to ensure that our hiring practices are inclusive and meet equal employment opportunity standards. Individuals looking for employment at Databricks are considered without regard to age, color, disability, ethnicity, family or marital status, gender identity or expression, language, national origin, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, veteran status, and other protected characteristics.</p> <p><strong>Compliance</strong></p> <p><strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">If access to export-controlled technology or source code is required for performance of job duties, it is within Employer's discretion whether to apply for a U.S. government license for such positions, and Employer may decline to proceed with an applicant on this basis alone.</span></strong></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
description: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About the Role You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems. The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model. What You'll Do Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data. 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP. Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production. Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling. Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems. Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate. What You'll Bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience. Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area. Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion. The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy). Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines. Nice to Have PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued. A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS. Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors. Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data. Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery. Compensation & Benefits Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. Location & Work Model This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office. We welcome applications from candidates who require visa sponsorship. Inclusive Application We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we're looking for. This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard. About us AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one. We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team. The role You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates. Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift. Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on. Your first 90 days FIRST 30 DAYS ◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run. ◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it. DAYS 30 TO 60 ◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria. ◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you. DAYS 60 TO 90 ◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround. ◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation. Who you are You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run. The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week. We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you. MUST HAVE ◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard. ◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number. ◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation. ◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you. ◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience. NICE TO HAVE ◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade. ◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays. ◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it. ◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation. ◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification. Why this is unusual Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product. That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it. Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are. How we work This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building. We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows. The team you will join You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on. We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work. Our process Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand. If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide. title: Computational Chemist (gn) @ Chemistry AI Venture, London
description: This an Atlantic portfolio venture. About the Venture This early-stage venture is building a discovery engine for chemistry, comprising a platform for running end-to-end simulations of chemical reaction systems, and a world model + agent stack that uses the simulation platform to discover new chemistry. Their goal is to build backend scientific data infrastructure to meet the demands of AI systems that can truly accelerate and automate the discovery layer of chemistry. Both founders hold PhDs in Chemistry from the University of Oxford, and the venture has already secured pre-seed funding. They are now building out their founding team. The Role As a Computational Chemist, you will play a central role in shaping the scientific foundations of the venture's technology, helping develop the computational methods and workflows that underpin its end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving progress towards the venture's strategic and scientific objectives. You’ll take ownership of developing, validating and optimising the computational chemistry components of the platform, with a particular focus on reaction mechanisms, reaction kinetics, molecular dynamics and the modelling of complex chemical environments. You will design, implement and refine scalable scientific workflows for generating, processing and analysing chemical reaction data, improving the accuracy, reliability and computational efficiency of simulations. Beyond your core scientific responsibilities, the team is looking for someone who can contribute to strategic research decisions, bring strong independent scientific judgement, and help shape the interdisciplinary research culture of the company at an early stage. What You'll Work On Foundation models for chemical reactivity: The team is building and training foundation models for chemical reactivity with a variety of data modalities. You'll help curate this foundational data corpus by developing cheminformatics and computational chemistry workflows for generating data from combinatorial enumeration, as well as robust data filtering, clustering and validation routines. Computational methods: The team is working on efficient computational methods from which foundational data is generated and the platform is validated. You'll be responsible for developing protocols for estimating solvation and entropy factors in chemical reaction steps. This involves keeping up to date with published literature for ideas and inspiration. Generative models: The venture is expanding its foundational data corpus beyond combinatorial workflows. You'll help design, validate and benchmark the generative model architectures that accomplish this. Chemical reaction simulation: The team is building out an end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You'll be involved in designing the architecture and assembling the platform, as well as developing benchmarks and validation protocols against computational and experimental methods. World models and agents: The venture will be developing an agent + world model stack that operates on the simulation platform. You'll be responsible for formulating the action space in which the world model is trained and the agent explores new chemical reaction space. What They're Looking For The team is looking for someone who enjoys being given a blank canvas and the chance to create something spectacular with it. In particular, someone who brings: A PhD in Computational Chemistry, Machine Learning, or a related field. Intellectual curiosity: Someone who enjoys venturing outside their comfort zone, exploring new ideas and applying their knowledge and experience to unfamiliar domains. An entrepreneurial mindset: Someone who thrives in an early-stage environment, enjoys building things from scratch and is excited to grow beyond the traditional boundaries of their role. Independent thinking and scientific judgement: Someone who can take ownership of complex challenges, contribute new ideas and help shape the scientific direction of the venture. A collaborative approach: Someone who can build strong relationships across the team and actively contribute to shaping and nurturing the company culture as it grows. An instinct for building great working environments: Someone who understands the importance of the right tools, systems and ways of working to help themselves and the wider team do their best work. title: Quality Systems Lead
description: About us Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production. Trusted by Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline, and more. We're an ambitious team of 100+ working at the frontier of AI and have raised $60M in Series C funding from Wellington Management, CRV, Next47 and Y Combinator. The role We're hiring a Quality Systems Lead to own how Encord measures the quality of the human data we deliver to frontier AI labs, physical AI companies and enterprise AI teams — the standard itself, the systems that evaluate against it, and the audit function that produces the ground truth behind both. Data quality is what our customers buy. As we scale across data types — image and video, document, medical, LLM evaluation, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — quality coverage cannot scale linearly with headcount. So this role has two halves that make each other work. You will build automated evaluation: model-assisted and LLM-based screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output. And you will build and run a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists in India, whose judgements become the labelled ground truth that trains and calibrates that automated layer. As coverage automates, the audit team moves up to the cases models can't judge and to generating gold sets for each new data type we take on. It is an unusual combination — engineering and consistent QC operations in one person — and it is the combination the job needs. You will also have an advantage your counterparts elsewhere in the industry don't: Encord owns the platform this work runs on, so the measurement you build can become native capability in the product rather than internal tooling. What you'll do Build automated dataset quality evaluation and root-cause detection — model-assisted and LLM-as-judge screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output Hire, train, calibrate and manage a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists based in our India operation, held to inter-rater agreement and catch rate rather than volume audited Turn audit output into labelled ground truth that trains and validates the automated layer, and manage the ratio of automated to manual coverage deliberately over time Own the quality standard for every data type we deliver — written rubrics with worked edge cases, golden sets, and acceptance criteria agreed with the customer, alongside the Special Projects lead, before the first batch ships Build scoring systems that rank annotator and reviewer performance and feed routing, staffing and offboarding decisions Set the pass thresholds that certification gates on, so nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard Report quality KPIs to leadership, and into the reporting our Special Projects leads take to customers: accuracy against client spec, inter-annotator agreement, rework rate, cost of rework, and coverage Work with Project Management on remediation — you produce the measurement and the diagnosis, production owns fixing the project, and the standard stays independent of the people being measured Own the unit economics of quality: cost per audited unit, and the coverage you buy per pound spent Partner with Product and Engineering to bring quality measurement into Encord platform as native capability Who we're looking for You build and you operate. You'll write the evaluation pipeline, and you'll also run the weekly calibration session with ten auditors in another country Your instinct on a coverage problem is to automate it — you reach for a model, a heuristic or a better sampling design before you reach for more auditors Statistically literate in a practical way: sampling design, agreement statistics, and the judgement to spot a metric being optimised against rather than met You can hold a calibrated standard across a distributed team you don't sit with — you know that ten uncalibrated auditors produce ten standards A strong writer. Much of this job is producing rubrics a distributed workforce can follow without you in the room You hold a standard under commercial pressure, and you bring the evidence that makes it stick with a delivery team or a client Systems thinker: as interested in why a failure recurs across projects as in this project's defect rate Experience requirements 4+ years owning both technical and operational outcomes in a data, AI or service delivery environment where quality was measured rather than asserted Hands-on Python and SQL. You build the analysis and the tooling rather than specify it for someone else Practical experience applying models to a quality or evaluation problem — LLM-as-judge, model-assisted QA, automated evaluation, anomaly detection or classifier-based screening Sampling methodology and agreement statistics (Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, F1 against ground truth) applied to real production data Experience hiring, training and managing a team, ideally an audit, review or QA team, and ideally distributed Track record of building a quality framework or function, including the reporting leadership and customers run on Bonus: direct experience of annotation, evaluation or model-training workflows, and of what frontier AI labs accept as evidence of quality Bonus: a STEM degree, or a background in data science or research engineering Bonus: multilingual delivery and linguistic quality assessment Why Encord Competitive salary, commission, and equity in a high-growth startup Strong in-person culture — most of the team works from our London office 4+ days/week 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays Annual learning & development budget Travel for customer visits, events, and conferences across the UK and Europe Company lunches twice a week Monthly socials & bi-annual team offsites Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Data Scientist
description: ABOUT BEAMERY With the rapid expansion of AI and automation, the future of work has never been more challenging for organizations. Beamery’s unique jobs, skills and tasks data platform helps organizations navigate these challenges and make more informed decisions across Talent Lifecycle Management. Our solutions power recruitment, mobility, upskilling, diversity, work architecture and workforce planning for some of the world’s most forward-thinking companies. We believe that where you work is much more than just a job. Millions of people are being left behind every day in their careers, and we’re on a mission to fix this by creating equal access to meaningful work, skills and careers for all. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to building a representative Beamery, creating an equitable, inclusive and engaging environment for our people. So, what are you waiting for? Join us and help us transform the future of work once and for all. What’s ahead — and why it’s an exciting time to join the team: Building agentic AI with advanced orchestration (multi-agent workflows, tool use, evaluation loops) that turns complex talent data into decisions. Training and fine-tuning our own models on unique data about jobs, skills and tasks, and benchmarking them against the best in our market. Joining an award-winning AI team (ACM RecSys Challenge 2026) that turns new ideas into innovative solutions with scientific rigour. Sharing our work and learning from industry peers through challenges, conferences and publications. But it’s not all about creating high-quality products, we also very much value the company culture we have worked hard to create; built on trust, empathy & honesty ensuring our workforce is able to bring their full selves to work. At the heart of our work is the Beamery taxonomy, the language of work (skills, role titles and tasks) that every Beamery product speaks, built on more than a decade of research and kept current by the Taxonomist, our agentic system, so it reflects the real pulse of the job market. You will be responsible for the full cycle of your work, from defining how quality is measured and designing the models to running robust scientific experiments, tracking technical and business metrics, and writing and reviewing code. You will also advise the product teams on how to implement AI features with an evaluation-first mindset, and keep pushing the boundaries of Beamery's AI. A strong foundation in NLP and GenAI, including Transformers, LLMs and embedding models (training or fine-tuning them is a strong plus). The ability to simplify complex problems, to work with ambiguity, and to collaborate with data scientists, engineers, product managers and business stakeholders. A Master's degree or PhD, or equivalent experience, in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics or a related field. Nice to Have Experience with explainable or conversational recommendations. Build and execute acquisition strategies tailored to the Pakistani community, using data and insight to optimise against KPIs and cut what is not working fast. Lead community-driven initiatives - events, meetups, forums - that build genuine trust and advocacy for LemFi, not just brand awareness for its own sake. Identify, negotiate, and manage partnerships with organisations and businesses that move the needle on user growth, ensuring every partnership delivers measurable value. Conduct ongoing market research to understand what your users actually need, and turn those insights into clear, actionable recommendations for Product and Marketing. Serve as the internal voice of the user - represent community perspectives in decisions about features, messaging, and positioning, and push back when LemFi gets it wrong. Use AI tools to streamline research, content, and reporting so more of your time goes to high-impact work in the field and less to admin. Strong cultural awareness and understanding of the Pakistani diaspora community in the UK, with the ability to build authentic trust with diverse stakeholders. Nice to have Experience working in or with remittance, fintech, or financial services products. Whether designing products, scaling operations, or telling our story, you’ll tackle complex challenges with real, immediate impact.
